parsed.elsewhere_quote:
Consequently the new board product is \(P'=P/g\).

- If \(g>1\), then \(P'<P\).
- If \(g=1\), the new entries are \(1\) and \(mn\). Thus \(P'=P\), while exactly two nonunits have been replaced by one, so \(K'=K-1\).
parsed.explanation: The displayed equality \(\operatorname{lcm}(m,n)=mn/g^2\) is false; it should be \(mn/g\). The surrounding proof nevertheless states and uses the correct board-product update \(P'=P/g\), then handles both \(g>1\) and \(g=1\), proves well-founded descent, and separately proves exactly one nonunit survives. Replacing the exponent 2 by 1 repairs the display.
